# Stress Rules

## Phase
Phase A — active from day 1.

## The Rules
Spanish stress placement is predictable from spelling. Learn these five rules and you can stress any word correctly.

**Rule 1 — Default for words ending in a vowel, -n, or -s:**
Stress falls on the **second-to-last syllable** (penultimate).

| Word | Syllables | Stress |
|------|-----------|--------|
| hablo | hab-lo | **HAB**-lo |
| comen | co-men | **CO**-men |
| libros | lib-ros | **LIB**-ros |
| casa | ca-sa | **CA**-sa |
| hablan | hab-lan | **HAB**-lan |

**Rule 2 — Default for words ending in any other consonant:**
Stress falls on the **last syllable**.

| Word | Syllables | Stress |
|------|-----------|--------|
| hablar | hab-lar | hab-**LAR** |
| ciudad | ciu-dad | ciu-**DAD** |
| comer | co-mer | co-**MER** |
| español | es-pa-ñol | es-pa-**ÑOL** |
| feliz | fe-liz | fe-**LIZ** |

**Rule 3 — Accent mark (tilde) overrides rules 1 and 2:**
When a word carries a written accent (´), stress that syllable, regardless of word ending.

| Word | Syllables | Stress |
|------|-----------|--------|
| teléfono | te-lé-fo-no | te-**LÉ**-fo-no |
| café | ca-fé | ca-**FÉ** |
| inglés | in-glés | in-**GLÉS** |
| árbol | ár-bol | **ÁR**-bol |
| jamás | ja-más | ja-**MÁS** |

**Rule 4 — Question and exclamation words always carry an accent:**
`qué`, `cómo`, `dónde`, `cuándo`, `cuál`, `quién`, `cuánto`, `por qué`

The accent signals interrogative or exclamatory use. The same word without an accent has a different grammatical function (see Rule 5).

**Rule 5 — Accents that distinguish meaning between identical-looking words:**

| Without accent | With accent | Distinction |
|---------------|-------------|-------------|
| si | sí | if / yes |
| el | él | the / he |
| tu | tú | your / you |
| como | cómo | like, as / how |
| mas | más | but (archaic) / more |
| se | sé | reflexive pronoun / I know |
| de | dé | of, from / give (subjunctive) |
| solo | sólo | alone / only (accent now optional per RAE) |

## Common English Speaker Errors

**Applying English stress patterns.** English stress is less predictable and often front-loaded. Spanish learners may stress the wrong syllable by feel rather than by rule (e.g., "tele-FO-no" instead of "te-LE-fo-no").

**Ignoring accent marks.** Beginners often treat the tilde as decoration. It carries grammatical information — misreading it changes stress and sometimes meaning.

**Not hearing stress differences.** In English, unstressed syllables are reduced (schwa), making stress very audible. In Spanish, all syllables are full, so stress differences are subtler. Train active listening for which syllable is longer and slightly louder.

**Confusing meaning-pairs.** Reading `si` when the text says `sí`, or `como` when it says `cómo`, produces grammatically incorrect sentences.

## Minimal Pairs
These pairs are identical except for the accent mark, which shifts stress and changes meaning.

| Without accent | With accent | Meanings |
|---------------|-------------|---------|
| papa | papá | potato / dad |
| como | cómo | as, like / how |
| si | sí | if / yes |
| el | él | the / he |
| tu | tú | your / you |
| mas | más | but (formal/archaic) / more |
| se | sé | reflexive pronoun / I know |
| solo | sólo | alone / only |

## Practice Assignments

**Speechling recordings:**
- Record minimal accent pairs back-to-back: `papa–papá`, `como–cómo`, `si–sí`
- Record Rule 1 words: `hablo`, `comen`, `libros`, `casa`, `trabajan`
- Record Rule 2 words: `hablar`, `ciudad`, `comer`, `español`, `feliz`
- Record tilde-override words: `teléfono`, `café`, `árbol`, `inglés`, `también`

**Stress identification exercises (tutor-led):**
Tutor says a word aloud; learner identifies the stressed syllable by tapping, saying the syllable number, or repeating with exaggerated stress on the correct syllable. Target words: `teléfono`, `hablar`, `libros`, `café`, `ciudad`, `comen`, `árbol`, `también`, `fácil`, `jamás`.

**Reading practice:**
Take a short paragraph. Before reading aloud, mark the stressed syllable in every word. Check rule application, then read and record.

## Signs of Acquisition
- Correctly stresses the penultimate syllable in rule-1 words without hesitation.
- Correctly stresses the final syllable in rule-2 words without hesitation.
- Reads accent marks and shifts stress accordingly, including tilde-override cases.
- Distinguishes meaning-changing accent pairs (`si/sí`, `el/él`, `tu/tú`) correctly in context.
- Speechling coach no longer flags stress errors in recorded words.
